landmarks.name: Great Pyramid of Khufu
landmarks.blurb: Built c. 2560 BC for Pharaoh Khufu. 2.3 million blocks, originally 146.6 m tall — the tallest human structure for ~3,800 years.

landmarks.name: Pyramid of Khafre
landmarks.blurb: Built c. 2570 BC for Khafre. Appears taller than Khufu's pyramid only because it stands on higher bedrock. Keeps its original Tura limestone casing near the summit.

landmarks.name: Pyramid of Menkaure
landmarks.blurb: Built c. 2510 BC for Menkaure, the smallest of the three. Its lowest courses were clad in red Aswan granite.

landmarks.name: Marriott Mena House
landmarks.blurb: The palace wing of the Mena House: a khedival hunting lodge of 1869, a hotel since 1886, at the foot of the plateau. Churchill, Roosevelt and Chiang Kai-shek met here in 1943. Most of the hotel lies just beyond the edge of this map.

landmarks.name: Mena House golf course
landmarks.blurb: Sixteen hectares of fairways between the hotel and Nazlet el-Semman — a golf course in the shadow of the Great Pyramid since 1899.

landmarks.name: Old Mena House gate
landmarks.blurb: The old ticket office on the road up from the Mena House. Until April 2025 this was the main way in; the entrance is now the Great Gate on the Fayoum road, 2.4 km west.

landmarks.name: Sphinx gate
landmarks.blurb: The ticket checkpoint at the foot of the Sphinx, facing the village. Since 2025 visitors mostly leave here rather than enter.

landmarks.name: KFC and Pizza Hut
landmarks.blurb: The most photographed fast-food branch in Egypt: its upper windows look straight across the plaza at the Sphinx.

landmarks.name: Guardian Guest House
landmarks.blurb: Four floors, ten rooms, no lift — and a roof terrace directly opposite the Sphinx entrance. One of a row of small inns along Abu al-Hol street.

landmarks.name: Pyramids View Inn
landmarks.blurb: One of the roof-terrace guest houses of Nazlet el-Semman, sold on the view of all three pyramids at breakfast.

landmarks.name: Panorama Pyramids Inn
landmarks.blurb: Another of the inns facing the Sphinx, with a rooftop café.

landmarks.name: Sound and Light theatre
landmarks.blurb: The open-air terrace of seats where audiences watch the evening Sound and Light show play over the Sphinx and the pyramids — as they have since 1961.

landmarks.name: Nazlet el-Semman stables
landmarks.blurb: The village has kept horses and camels for visitors for generations; the yards lie behind the houses. Since 2025 the animals work only in set zones on the south side of the plateau.

landmarks.name: St George's Church
landmarks.blurb: The Coptic church of Mar Girgis, Nazlet el-Semman.

landmarks.name: King Farouk's rest house
landmarks.blurb: A small royal rest house on the edge of the plateau north-east of the Great Pyramid, built for King Farouk in the 1940s.

landmarks.name: 9 Pyramids Lounge
landmarks.blurb: An open-air restaurant on the southern ridge, opened in October 2020: 1.3 km from the Great Pyramid, looking north at all of them.

landmarks.name: Khufu's restaurant
landmarks.blurb: A restaurant in the King Khufu Centre on the western approach, part of the 2025 redevelopment of the visitor route.

landmarks.name: Visitor bus stop — Panorama
landmarks.blurb: A stop on the free electric hop-on hop-off bus line that has carried visitors round the plateau since April 2025, when private cars, taxis and tour coaches were barred from the site.

landmarks.name: Visitor bus stop — Menkaure
landmarks.blurb: The visitor bus stop for the Third Pyramid.

landmarks.name: Visitor bus stop — Khafre
landmarks.blurb: The visitor bus stop for the Second Pyramid.

landmarks.name: Visitor bus stop — Khufu
landmarks.blurb: The visitor bus stop for the Great Pyramid.

landmarks.name: Visitor bus stop — Sphinx
landmarks.blurb: The visitor bus stop at the Sphinx, by the exit to the village.

landmarks.name: The Great Sphinx
landmarks.blurb: A 73 m limestone sphinx with the body of a lion and a royal human head, generally attributed to the reign of Khafre.

landmarks.name: Sphinx Temple
landmarks.blurb: Built of blocks quarried from around the Sphinx itself — an open court ringed by granite-cased pillars, aligned with the equinox sunrise.

landmarks.name: Khafre Valley Temple
landmarks.blurb: Khafre's granite-clad valley temple beside the Sphinx, at the foot of his causeway — its pillared hall held his great seated statues.

landmarks.name: Temple of Amenhotep II
landmarks.blurb: A mud-brick chapel built ~1,100 years after the pyramids by Amenhotep II, who worshipped the Sphinx as Horemakhet, "Horus in the Horizon".

landmarks.name: Khufu Mortuary Temple
landmarks.blurb: Only the black basalt pavement of Khufu's mortuary temple survives — its limestone walls were carried off as building stone.

landmarks.name: Khafre Mortuary Temple
landmarks.blurb: The most complete Old Kingdom mortuary temple: entrance hall, pillared court and five statue niches, built of colossal local limestone blocks.

landmarks.name: Menkaure Valley Temple
landmarks.blurb: Menkaure's valley temple at the foot of his causeway — begun in stone and finished in mud brick after his death.

landmarks.name: Khufu Valley Temple
landmarks.blurb: Khufu's valley temple at the east end of his causeway — its remains lie buried beneath the modern village of Nazlet el-Samman.

landmarks.name: Central Field Quarry (GIS)
landmarks.blurb: The main quarry south of the Great Pyramid, where workers cut the core limestone blocks — leaving stepped benches in the bedrock.

landmarks.name: Menkaure Quarry
landmarks.blurb: Quarry faces and channels south-east of Menkaure — the source of his core blocks, still showing the trenches where stones were levered free.

landmarks.name: Tomb of Khentkaus I
landmarks.blurb: The "Fourth Pyramid of Giza" — the two-tiered rock-cut tomb of Queen Khentkaus I, at the head of the Central Field.

landmarks.name: Workers' Town (Heit el-Ghurab)
landmarks.blurb: Heit el-Ghurab, the "Lost City of the Pyramids": barracks, bakeries and long galleries that housed the crews who built Giza.

landmarks.name: Wall of the Crow
landmarks.blurb: A massive limestone wall (~200 m long, ~10 m high) with a monumental gateway between the plateau and the workers' town.

landmarks.name: Khufu Satellite Pyramid (G1-d)
landmarks.blurb: A small satellite (cult) pyramid for the king's ka.

landmarks.name: Khafre Satellite Pyramid (G II-a)
landmarks.blurb: A small satellite (cult) pyramid for the king's ka.

landmarks.name: Khufu's Solar Boat
landmarks.blurb: A nod to the 43 m cedar "solar barque" found dismantled in a sealed pit beside the Great Pyramid in 1954 and painstakingly reassembled.

landmarks.name: Trial Passages
landmarks.blurb: Rock-cut passages east of the Great Pyramid that reproduce its internal corridors at near-full scale — likely a builders' mock-up.

landmarks.name: Khentkaus Town
landmarks.blurb: A settlement of priests who served the cult of Queen Khentkaus I, built against her monument.

landmarks.name: Workers' Cemetery
landmarks.blurb: Tombs of the pyramid builders on the slope above their town — small mud-brick and stone tombs, some with miniature vaulted superstructures.

artifacts.name: Sarcophagus lid fragment
artifacts.blurb: A corner of the red-granite lid that was already gone when Caliph al-Ma'mun's men forced their way in (AD 820).

artifacts.name: Copper fitting from the shaft
artifacts.blurb: Like the copper 'handles' found on the door-slab at the top of the Queen's Chamber shaft by the Upuaut robot in 1993.

artifacts.name: Tomb robber's oil lamp
artifacts.blurb: A pottery saucer lamp of the kind carried by the medieval explorers who scrambled down to the unfinished Subterranean Chamber.

artifacts.name: Quarryman's copper chisel
artifacts.blurb: Copper chisels and dolerite pounders were the only metal tools available; they were resharpened constantly.

artifacts.name: Ushabti of Thutmose IV
artifacts.blurb: Thutmose IV cleared the Sphinx of sand around 1400 BC after a dream, and raised the Dream Stele between its paws.

artifacts.name: Diorite chip from a Khafre statue
artifacts.blurb: Khafre's famous seated statue (Cairo Museum) was found buried in a pit in this valley temple in 1860.

artifacts.name: Greywacke triad fragment
artifacts.blurb: Reisner found Menkaure's triad statues — the king with Hathor and a nome goddess — here in 1908.

artifacts.name: Bread mould (bedja)
artifacts.blurb: Thousands of these conical bread pots were found in the bakeries of the workers' town beyond the Wall of the Crow.

artifacts.name: Beer jar
artifacts.blurb: Workers were paid in bread and beer — roughly ten loaves and a jug or two a day.

artifacts.name: Faience amulet
artifacts.blurb: Blue-green faience amulets were buried with the priests who served Queen Khentkaus' cult.

artifacts.name: Wooden set-square
artifacts.blurb: The Trial Passages were the builders' full-size mock-up; set-squares and plumb lines kept the angles true.

artifacts.name: Basalt paving block
artifacts.blurb: Black basalt from the Fayum paved the floors of Khufu's temples — the same stone as the causeway pavement.

artifacts.name: Dolerite pounder
artifacts.blurb: Hard dolerite balls were used to bash out the limestone blocks in the Central Field quarry.

artifacts.name: Painted false-door fragment
artifacts.blurb: The workers' tombs had tiny false doors so the dead could receive offerings — same idea as the nobles' mastabas.

artifacts.name: Tura casing chip
artifacts.blurb: Khafre still keeps its fine white Tura limestone casing near the summit; the rest was stripped for medieval Cairo.

artifacts.name: Aswan granite spall
artifacts.blurb: Menkaure's lower sixteen courses were cased in red granite shipped 900 km down the Nile from Aswan.

artifacts.name: Pyramidion fragment
artifacts.blurb: The Great Pyramid lost its capstone long ago; today the summit is a flat platform ~8 m below the original apex.
